questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The nature surrounding Bergen and the cultural experiences that Bergen has to offer (especially when it comes to art and music).

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy! Bergen University is very good at making information accessible and they are very helpful if you send them a mail with questions!

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: They have a student information center, where they can help you! And they were also very helpful when we were at an intromeeting one of the first days. I also missed the deadline for exam registration, but they were very sweet and helpful with signing me up for the exam!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Quite easy! I found housing on
hybel.no
!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I would really recommend living off campus, near the city centre, and definitely preferably with Norwegians! It made it much easier to get to know Norwegians and to learn the language and the culture better. Highly recommend, as on-campus living is almost purely exchange students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Bergen University is very well organized, so I got emails with clear instructions every time some form of registration was necessary.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The student centre is always easy to contact.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesful! It was very easy. Just be aware that you also sign up for the exam, as this is not a given.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Remember to check your email!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took 2 BA-classes, and the lectures were really good, well-structured and high-level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I think at times difficult topics were made more understandable as the level of explanation was a little more simple.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: PSYK106 (personnell psychology) and KUVI106 (kjønn, seksualitet og kultur).

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Definitely KUVI106!! Kjønn, seksualitet og kultur was the best course I'v ever had. Such a sweet and amazing lexturerer who does all the lectures, which creates a really good correspondence between all the lectures. Lots of great class discussions, really interactive and high level theories (Foucault, Judith Butler, Sarah Ahmed) explained in a really really good way! I learned so much.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: My phone subscription at Oister started costing a lot after 3 months outside Denmark, so they charged me for all data I used. I would recommend changing your subscription to Greenspeak as they don't change how much they charge you, despite you being outside Denmark for a long time. That way you don't have to get a norwegian phone subscription.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food and alcohol is really expensive. Especially eating out.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I joined Mørkerommet, which is a photography collective that has their own dark room on campus, to develop film! It was really cheap to join and every month they had 'beer and develop' events, where people meet up, develop film and hang out. Super nice people and they had exhibitions and a magazine launch. I also joined the sammen gym, which is really cheap and gives access to a swimmingpool, fitness centres, team sports etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to museums and local cultural events! And definitely go hiking!!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go hiking!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy as it is similar to danish culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join mørkerommet and become a volunteer at Laugaren sauna!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Sometimes the language barrierer would make conversations lose their flow, but people were generally very patient and motivated to understand danish better, so often it was just a really cute scandinavian experience <3

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The way the Norwegians use the nature and are super open and friendly on hikes <3

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Pick classes that you find intriguing and be aware of the amount of obligatory activities! The courses I chose had no assignments or obligatory classes, so I had a lot of freedom and spent most of my time on hikes hehe.
2. Use the nature as much as possible, especially when the weather is good<3 Hike all 7 fjells and take the train outside Bergen to see Finse, Hallingskeid and Myrdal!
3. Go in the spring, as it rains a lot less!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't let the rain stop you from going to Bergen, but I would highly recommend going in the spring <3

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I met the most amazing Norwegians from a big friendgroup, and they were so warm, welcoming and open and I became a part of the group. It really warmed my heart that I made friends with them and we hung out a lot, and it was just so rewarding to make new friends <3

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I think I would have found it very challenging to be on my own, but I went to Bergen with 2 friends from home, so I didn't feel homesick really. Would highly recommend <3

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
